It sounds like your microwave’s turntable motor or the drive mechanism has failed, but the magnetron (the part that generates heat) is still working fine. This is a very common issue and usually easy to fix.

### Why this happens:
• The turntable doesn’t rotate, so food only gets exposed to one "hot spot" in the microwave field → one side hot, one side cold.
• The motor that spins the plate may have burned out, or the plastic gear/coupler underneath has cracked or slipped.

---

### ✅ What You Can Do:

#### 1. Check for Obvious Issues
• Make sure the turntable glass isn’t cracked or warped.
• Ensure it’s seated correctly on the roller ring and center spindle.
• Clean any food debris under the plate that might be jamming it.

#### 2. Test the Turntable Motor
• Remove the glass plate and the roller ring underneath.
• Look at the small plastic coupler (a little gear-like piece) in the center of the microwave floor.
• Try turning it by hand — if it spins freely but the motor doesn’t engage, the motor may be dead.
• If you hear a humming sound when starting the microwave but nothing moves, the motor or gears are likely stuck/broken.

#### 3. Replace the Turntable Motor or Coupler
• These parts are inexpensive ($10–$25) and widely available online (search for your microwave model + “turntable motor” or “drive coupler”).
• Replacement is usually straightforward: unplug the microwave, remove a few screws, swap out the part, and reassemble.

#### 4. Workaround (If You Don’t Want to Repair)
• Manually rotate the plate halfway through cooking.
• Stir or rearrange food mid-way through heating.
• Use a microwave-safe plate on top of the turntable and rotate it by hand if needed.

---

### ⚠️ Safety Note:
• Always unplug the microwave before inspecting or replacing any internal parts.
• If you’re uncomfortable opening the unit, consider calling a repair technician — though this is often not cost-effective for older microwaves.

That confirms it: the drive coupler (the 3-pronged plastic piece) has failed. This is a very common failure point in Sharp microwaves like your R272WM. The motor still works, but it can’t transfer power to the turntable because the coupler is broken.

### ✅ Solution: Replace the Drive Coupler

#### 🔧 Part You Need:
• Sharp Microwave Turntable Drive Coupler
  • Often listed as part number: Y108-003547 or similar (varies slightly by batch).
  • Compatible with Sharp R272WM and many other Sharp models.

#### 💰 Cost:
• Usually $5–$15 online (Amazon, eBay, PartsTown, etc.).

---

### 🛠️ How to Replace It (Step-by-Step):

1. Unplug the microwave.
   ⚠️ Never work on a plugged-in appliance.

2. Remove the glass turntable and roller ring.
   Lift them straight up — they’re usually just sitting on top of the coupler.

3. Access the drive coupler:
   • On most Sharp models, you need to remove the bottom cover or rear panel to access the motor assembly.
   • For the R272WM:
• Remove 4–6 screws from the back/bottom of the microwave.
• Gently lift off the outer casing (careful with wires).
• Locate the turntable motor — it’s a small cylindrical component with a shaft sticking up.

4. Remove the broken coupler:
   • The coupler snaps onto the motor shaft. It may be held by a clip or just friction.
   • Pull it straight off (it might require gentle wiggling).

5. Install the new coupler:
   • Align the 3 prongs with the slots on the motor shaft.
   • Press firmly until it snaps into place and sits flush.

6. Reassemble:
   • Put the casing back on and secure screws.
   • Replace the roller ring and glass plate.
   • Plug in and test — the turntable should now rotate smoothly.

---

### 🔍 Tips:
• Take photos before disassembling so you remember screw/wire positions.
• If the motor itself feels stiff or doesn’t spin when you manually turn the coupler, the motor may also need replacing (less common).
• Use a multimeter to test motor continuity if unsure (not required for most users).

---

### 📦 Where to Buy:
• Amazon: Search “Sharp R272WM turntable drive coupler”
• eBay: Often cheaper with free shipping
• PartsTown.com or AppliancePartsPros.com: Reliable sources with diagrams

The coupler sits inside the microwave cavity, mounted directly onto the turntable motor shaft, and is not accessible from the top or through any external openings.
